kaigo-review-01-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Preserve the person’s participation conditions and ask their wishes again after checking return support and timing.
Distinguish explanations of knowledge from practical checks, and support provided from personal outcomes in the care process.

kaigo-review-01-knowledge-0.heading: Consent to participation and personal conditions
paragraphs: Participation itself is not the goal; ask how the person wants to spend time. Conditions such as ‘for a short time’ or ‘if I know help is available to return early’ are part of their wishes. Do not omit conditions and record consent to participate.
Respect choices to join, decline or decide after checking. After support conditions are arranged, ask current wishes again. Meeting conditions alone does not establish participation.

kaigo-review-01-knowledge-1.heading: Support before and after movement
paragraphs: Check return support as well as the outward trip, together with condition, abilities, surroundings, equipment and staff responsibility. Preparing a wheelchair does not establish that today’s condition and assistance needs were checked.
Communicating conditions in this material does not establish safe transfer or wheelchair skills. Actual methods follow the individual plan and training. Do not invent missing conditions and depart.

kaigo-review-01-knowledge-2.heading: Separate explaining reasons from practical assessment
paragraphs: Explain in your own words why brakes are checked, arms are not pulled and level changes are announced. Consider the risks avoided, such as wheelchair movement, bodily strain or inability to prepare for sudden movement.

Explaining a reason differs from operating correctly. Apply knowledge to examples with different conditions; check practical skills individually under an appropriate instructor. Do not start unfamiliar assistance from text alone.

kaigo-review-01-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] Morikawa-san wants to hear a little music but not stay until the end. They want return support and timing checked before deciding. They remain in their room; neither departure nor participation is decided. This is not practice in actual transport.

kaigo-review-02-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: For ordinary information sharing, distinguish consent to content, recipient and method.
With suspected abuse, separate confirmed facts and unknowns and distinguish internal reporting from notification to the municipality.

kaigo-review-02-knowledge-0.heading: Family relationships and information-sharing scope
paragraphs: Family may be important supporters, but being family does not authorize every record by every method. Check confirmed consent and facility procedures for content, recipient, purpose and method.

Consent to explanation in a meeting does not extend to recording, sending record photos or using private messages. This situation practices ordinary sharing, distinct from legally required abuse notification.

kaigo-review-02-knowledge-1.heading: Acknowledge concerns and establish facts
paragraphs: Even with physical assistance needs, relationships, recognition and personal choice still matter. Listen to personal and family concerns and acknowledge feelings while distinguishing confirmed facts.
Forgetting schedules or difficulty expressing words does not remove the need to hear wishes. Offer suitable communication, questions and response time to support choice.

kaigo-review-02-knowledge-2.heading: Explanation and contact with responsible staff
paragraphs: Ask specifically what family wants and briefly explain known facts and unknowns. Tell the responsible person what is requested, which consent is unconfirmed and how the family wants the reply.
Do not promise personal-phone photos to reassure someone or send before checking. Distinguish receiving a request, asking for checks, deciding to send and actually sending.

kaigo-review-02-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] Megumi asks for photos of her mother’s activity record by private message. Only consent to discussion in a meeting with responsible staff is confirmed. Photo sharing and its method remain unconfirmed; nothing has been sent.

kaigo-review-03-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Distinguish posting and effective dates, and plans from completed actions.
Understand restraint through restrictions on personal freedom; do not act based only on family requests.

kaigo-review-03-knowledge-0.heading: Separate schedules, action records and change notices
paragraphs: Schedules show future activity; action records preserve actual events. A scheduled bath time does not establish completed bathing then. Check support for each action, such as eating and changing, separately.

A notice’s posting date may differ from when changes start. Accident records separate observed or heard events from unknown causes. Identify document type before reading whose information, when and what.

kaigo-review-03-knowledge-1.heading: Read multiple times and exceptions
paragraphs: Event start, staff preparation, incident occurrence and record-writing times may differ. Read subjects and verbs around times rather than numbers alone.
Preserve both general plans and person-specific conditions. Do not erase individual conditions to make everyone identical; ask staff about matters the document cannot establish.

kaigo-review-03-knowledge-2.heading: Draw evidence-based conclusions
paragraphs: Choose a short document and identify who does what, when and under which conditions. Summarize what it establishes in one sentence and write unknowns separately.
Do not turn plans into completed actions or unknowns into no abnormality. Practice reading evidence in another project-created document rather than memorizing questions and answers.

kaigo-review-03-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] On October 24, you check a laundry collection slip with Kishimoto-san. Today’s slip names the old storage room; a notice names the new room from the 25th. Practice effective dates, not independently rewriting procedures or moving items.

kaigo-review-04-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Use the person’s words to check location and sensation without leading them.
Distinguish unobserved, not connected and ongoing responses; do not delay calls for urgent changes.

kaigo-review-04-knowledge-0.heading: Separate body-part names from symptoms
paragraphs: Body location differs from symptoms such as pain, itching, numbness or swelling. ‘Around the mouth’ does not identify outer lip skin or inside the mouth. Check the indicated place, onset and sensation.
Avoid questions that decide a disease first and seek agreement. If explanation is difficult, use understandable words or gestures and report remaining uncertainty.

kaigo-review-04-knowledge-1.heading: Review the main organ functions
paragraphs: The heart pumps blood for circulation. The lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide; kidneys make urine and remove waste. The digestive tract digests and absorbs food and expels remaining material as stool.

Nerves carry information and instructions involved in bodily function. Endocrine hormones regulate functions; immunity protects against pathogens and other threats. Similar discomfort may have several factors. Knowing an organ name does not diagnose the cause.

kaigo-review-04-knowledge-2.heading: Adapt questions and record unknowns
paragraphs: Adapt questions to vision, hearing and language and allow response time. Do not record no redness without looking or normal values without measuring. Separate the person’s own words, observations and measurements.
Ordinary dialogue practice differs from a situation needing immediate help. With urgent changes, do not prioritize finishing every question; seek help, make necessary contact and follow instructions.

kaigo-review-04-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Practice situation created for this material] With nurse Fujino, consider ‘Around my mouth feels different’ in a fictional record. Outer skin versus inside is unknown, and nothing has been observed. This teaches questions and records, not actual examination or symptom assessment.

kaigo-depth-30.heading: Nails: routine care and conditions needing consultation
paragraphs: Unmaintained nails may collect dirt or scratch skin. Soft nails after bathing may be easier to handle, but that alone does not justify cutting. First inspect nails and surrounding skin, checking pain, swelling, inflammation and changes in thickness or color.

Whether routine nail care is appropriate depends on nail and skin abnormalities and any need for specialist disease management. Consult healthcare professionals when uncertain or abnormal and check staff scope and the individual plan.

Even when routine care is confirmed suitable, use clean, appropriate tools and arrange visibility and lighting. Avoid cutting too short or deeply into corners; use a nail file if needed. Do not pull painful fingers. Actual methods follow facility procedures and training.

Do not dig out the corner of a thick nail with a swollen, painful edge in an attempt to relieve it. A ‘no pain’ reply does not replace skin inspection. Treating abnormal nails from this text alone is outside this section’s scope.

kaigo-depth-31.heading: Makeup: personal choice and care afterward
paragraphs: Makeup can express individuality. Ask whether and what the person wants without assumptions about age or gender. Do not make makeup a condition of participation. Separate independent actions from help needed.

Place mirrors and tools accessibly and help only where needed in a comfortable posture. Confirm personal products and use, keeping them out of eyes and mouth. Do not replace skin treatment with cosmetics or use unchecked shared tools.

Wanting lipstick does not consent to every product, such as foundation. Avoid concealing redness and missing changes; stop and consult if changes occur. Before bed, remove makeup and care for skin according to habits and plan. Help where the person cannot do it independently.
This section teaches checking wishes and the care sequence. This explanation alone does not determine individual skin assessment or product suitability.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-intro.heading: Additional practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] With Kawase-san, review Morikawa-san’s reading-support record. The goal was choosing a favorite book and sharing impressions if participation was wanted. Staff prepared large-print books and a quiet seat under the plan. The person chose one, then wanted to read alone, so no sharing occurred. No new plan is decided.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-knowledge-0.heading: Assessment: gather and analyze information
paragraphs: The care process involves considering, providing and reviewing support for the life the person wants. Assessment gathers and analyzes wishes, abilities and difficulties. Do not make staff-preferred activities into personal goals.
Preserve both the wish to choose a book and the condition of still wanting to discuss it. Responses and new wishes also inform further thinking.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-knowledge-1.heading: Planning and implementation: identify what was done
paragraphs: Plans record information-based goals and specific support. Implementation means actually providing support, not copying the plan.
Preparing large-print books and a quiet seat is staff implementation; choosing a book is a confirmed personal outcome. Neither proves impressions were shared.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-knowledge-2.heading: Evaluation: consider conditions and personal outcomes
paragraphs: Evaluation considers whether support suited the person and how far outcomes met goals. Distinguish choosing a book from later wanting to read alone and not sharing impressions.

Do not label the person uncooperative for not sharing or record full achievement. The sharing goal depends on their wishes. Consider suitable current support with them rather than forcing participation.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-knowledge-3.heading: Discuss review based on new information
paragraphs: Results and current wishes may prompt more information and consultation about revising goals and support. Care-process stages are not completed once and never revisited.
Report facts for discussion with the person and team. Consultation alone does not approve a new goal, and a worker does not independently rewrite the plan.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-case.heading: Checks and scope for this situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] With Kawase-san, review Morikawa-san’s reading-support record. The goal was choosing a favorite book and sharing impressions if participation was wanted. Staff prepared large-print books and a quiet seat under the plan. The person chose one, then wanted to read alone, so no sharing occurred. No new plan is decided.
[Checks] Separate support provided, personal achievements, current wishes and undecided revisions. Do not formulate or approve plans from this material alone; consult the person and team.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-intro.heading: Additional practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] At an older-adult care facility, at 10:05 in the lounge, you hear a worker tell Hasebe-san, ‘If you call again, you won’t get lunch.’ The person is frightened and wants someone present. You call help; another worker is now with them. Injury and actual meal provision are unconfirmed. This is a report to Kawase; municipal notification is not yet made. The speaker is not identified as an existing colleague character.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-knowledge-0.heading: Respond to suspicion before injury status is established
paragraphs: Abuse includes not only physical assault but psychological harm, neglect, sexual acts and improper handling of property. Unconfirmed injury does not justify dismissing suspected abuse.
The confirmed fact is the threat to withhold food; actual lunch withholding is unknown. Do not invent an overall conclusion. Protect the person and make necessary notification.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-knowledge-1.heading: Separate heard words, personal accounts and responses
paragraphs: Accurately state when, where and whose words you heard. Reported fear differs from a worker-observed injury. Separate help called, current accompaniment and unknowns too.

Do not repeatedly make the person retell events or independently investigate the suspected worker to reach conclusions. If danger continues, seek safe help immediately rather than prioritizing long report practice.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-knowledge-2.heading: Distinguish internal reporting from municipal notification
paragraphs: Article 21(1) of Japan’s Act on Prevention of Elder Abuse applies to a worker discovering an older person thought to have been abused by staff of the care facility or service where that worker is engaged. Check the statutory scope, including facilities or services under the same operator. In such cases, prompt notification to the municipality is required.

Reporting to a supervisor does not complete municipal notification. Do not wait for conclusive investigation or make supervisor permission a condition. Communicate known facts and unknowns separately. This provision is not directly applied to every household situation.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-knowledge-3.heading: Do not confuse required notification with ordinary sharing
paragraphs: For notifications within this article, confidentiality laws are not interpreted as preventing notification. However, the article limits treatment of false or negligent notifications; do not invent facts or present unknowns as confirmed.

Notification differs from sending record photos to family or public social-media posting. Ordinary sharing stays within confirmed consent and methods. Meeting consent does not authorize recording or private-message delivery.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-case.heading: Checks and scope for this situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] At an older-adult care facility, at 10:05 in the lounge, you hear a worker tell Hasebe-san, ‘If you call again, you won’t get lunch.’ The person is frightened and wants someone present. You call help; another worker is now with them. Injury and actual meal provision are unconfirmed. This is a report to Kawase; municipal notification is not yet made. The speaker is not identified as an existing colleague character.

[Checks] Prioritize safety and separate heard facts from unknowns. This does not teach investigation, diagnosis or treatment. Distinguish ordinary sharing from statutory notification and do not promise undecided actions.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-intro.heading: Additional practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] At 1:40 p.m., Megumi asks for her mother Morikawa-san’s room to be locked from tonight so she cannot go out. It is a request; locking has not occurred. Personal wishes, specific danger, alternatives and organizational decisions are unknown. Consult Kawase without promising implementation. Do not add a diagnosis such as dementia.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-knowledge-0.heading: Look at freedom of action rather than labels
paragraphs: Consider restraint by whether freedom of action is restricted. Isolating someone in a room they cannot open to prevent leaving is an example. Calling it ‘for safety’ does not remove the restriction.
Do not uniformly classify every closed door or similar tool. Check purpose, actual conditions and personal effects. This example is an unimplemented request intended to prevent leaving.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-knowledge-1.heading: Family requests alone do not decide implementation
paragraphs: Listen to family concerns, but family requests or consent alone do not authorize restraint. Discuss wishes, safety and nonrestrictive support with relevant professionals.
Do not promise locking or independently change medication or equipment. Nor does this material authorize independently deciding and performing removal of an existing restriction.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-knowledge-2.heading: Restraint prohibited in principle; consider exceptions carefully
paragraphs: Restraint is prohibited in principle. Considering an unavoidable emergency exception requires all three conditions: imminent serious danger to life or body, no alternative and temporary duration. ‘Only briefly’ alone is insufficient.

Do not decide alone. Follow organizational procedures for careful discussion with the person, family and relevant people, explanation and records. Continue observation and reconsideration and remove restrictions immediately when criteria no longer apply. The team handles removal methods; this section teaches neither applying nor removing techniques.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-knowledge-3.heading: Accurately report requests, nonimplementation and unknowns
paragraphs: Clearly report who requested what, when and from when, and whether it was done. Report unknown wishes, dangers and alternatives as unknown for team and personal discussion. Receiving a request is not implementation approval.

If inappropriate restrictions raise suspected abuse, do not stop at internal consultation; check applicable notification provisions. Tomorrow’s change in routine form destination does not justify delaying today’s safety contact.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-case.heading: Checks and scope for this situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] At 1:40 p.m., Megumi asks for her mother Morikawa-san’s room to be locked from tonight so she cannot go out. It is a request; locking has not occurred. Personal wishes, specific danger, alternatives and organizational decisions are unknown. Consult Kawase without promising implementation. Do not add a diagnosis such as dementia.
[Checks] Focus on wishes and freedom. Family requests are not approval; individual workers do not independently decide application or removal.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-intro.heading: Additional practice situation
paragraphs: [Offline training situation] At 9:36, Hasebe-san suddenly has difficulty exerting force in the right arm but responds when called. The first 119 call is unconnected; Kishimoto has another phone. The fictional location is Hidamari Care, second-floor lounge,4-8-2 Higashimachi, Sakura Ward, Tokyo. Neither facility nor address is an actual emergency location. Do not actually call. Kishimoto reads colleague training cards, not the dispatcher role.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-knowle.heading: Request emergency help immediately for sudden one-sided weakness
paragraphs: Sudden weakness in one arm or leg is a symptom identified as requiring an immediate 119 ambulance request. Do not wait for a disease name or every question’s answer. Responding when called alone does not rule out urgency.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-knowle.heading: An attempted call differs from connection
paragraphs: If 119 does not connect, use another means such as a public phone or asking others. Here, immediately ask Kishimoto to use the other phone and check connection. Divide roles while keeping a worker beside the person.
Do not actually call 119 for an examination. This is offline practice; make needed calls only for real emergencies.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-knowle.heading: Give location and condition and follow instructions
paragraphs: State that an ambulance is needed, the address, facility, floor and room, and known condition. Mark unknown age or cause as unknown without inventing diagnoses or numbers. Give names, callback details and other information in response to dispatcher questions.

Follow the actual question order rather than waiting to memorize every example. After connecting, continue responding under first-aid and other necessary instructions. Connection does not mean all response is finished.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-knowle.heading: Separate ordinary questions from emergency situations
paragraphs: Questions about mouth or neck location are separate ordinary dialogue exercises, not instructions to complete them before requesting help for sudden weakness.

Even in ordinary practice, do not record unseen conditions as normal. If words are unclear, ask the person to indicate the place and report their words and the unobserved matters separately to the person responsible. Absence of these textbook symptoms alone does not rule out every emergency.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-case.heading: Checks and scope for this situation
paragraphs: [Offline training situation] At 9:36, Hasebe-san suddenly has difficulty exerting force in the right arm but responds when called. The first 119 call is unconnected; Kishimoto has another phone. The fictional location is Hidamari Care, second-floor lounge,4-8-2 Higashimachi, Sakura Ward, Tokyo. Neither facility nor address is an actual emergency location. Do not actually call. Kishimoto reads colleague training cards, not the dispatcher role.

[Checks] This training involves no actual call. In real emergencies, do not finish the training dialogue first; immediately request help and respond. Never use the fictional place as the true address.

kaigo-review-01-transfer-legacy.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] The person wants to join storytelling briefly if return assistance is confirmed. The shared schedule does not establish the individual return arrangements.

Ask about conditions, such as help needed to return early, and contact the responsible person before starting. Do not promise unknown times or helpers; explain results, then ask whether they want to join.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-transfer-legac.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] The plan is to choose a favorite song and listen together if wanted. Morikawa-san chose a song, but the activity has not started. They want support and timing for returning to the room at 2:25 p.m. checked before deciding; if conditions do not fit, they do not want to join.
Example question: ‘Would you like to decide about joining after we check support for returning to your room at 2:25 p.m.?’

Song choice does not decide participation or establish return support. Report conditions and check with staff, then explain results and ask the person’s choice. Do not independently approve new goals or change plans.

kaigo-review-02-transfer-legacy.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Another ordinary sharing situation] Family wants to record a meeting, but consent covers only receiving an explanation in person. Recording has not occurred.
Explain that recording is separate and check personal consent and facility procedures with staff. Do not extend meeting consent to recording or promise it before checking.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-transfer-legac.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Ordinary meeting separate from the abuse case] Megumi wants to record the activity explanation and receive photos by private message. Personal consent covers only a staff meeting explanation; recording and sending are unconfirmed and neither performed. Megumi requests checking with the person and receiving results at a meeting.

Example explanation: ‘Consent to a staff meeting explanation is confirmed. Recording and private-message photos remain unconfirmed and neither has occurred. I’ll ask staff to check with the person and explain results at the meeting.’

This is not municipal abuse notification. Do not reinterpret statutory notification rules as permission for family recordings or photos. Do not act before checking; preserve consent scope, recipient and method.

kaigo-review-03-transfer-legacy.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Document situation] Sunday’s slip gives the old meeting point; a notice gives a new one from Monday. Different applicable dates do not necessarily conflict.
Hand over Sunday separately from Monday onward, connecting effective dates and places. Ask staff about instructions with unclear dates rather than independently rewriting documents.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-transfer-legacy.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Document practice separate from the locking request] Today is Sunday. Today’s consultation form goes to the staff room; the notice says consultation room from Monday. An additional paper has no effective date, so whether it changes today’s slip is unclear. Today’s safety contact is needed immediately.

Example handoff: ‘Sunday’s destination is the staff room; from Monday it is the consultation room. The extra paper has no effective date, so I’ll check with staff. I won’t independently change today’s slip, and I’ll make today’s safety contact immediately.’
Separate routine form submission from necessary safety contact. Do not interpret the notice as waiting until tomorrow or confuse it with deciding restraint application, removal or exceptions.

kaigo-review-04-transfer-legacy.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Another ordinary dialogue exercise] The person says, ‘Around my neck feels different.’ Outer skin versus inside the throat is unknown, and nothing has been observed.
Example question: ‘Which part around your neck feels different?’ Listen without first deciding it is a skin or throat disease.
Report the person’s words separately from unknown precise location and observation results. Do not record unobserved conditions as normal or without abnormality.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-transf.heading: Consider another situation
paragraphs: [Separate ordinary dialogue, not a step before emergency requests] Onodera-san reports an unusual sensation around the neck. Outer skin versus inside the throat is unknown; no observation has occurred.
Example question: ‘Which part around your neck feels different?’

Example report to Kawase: ‘Onodera-san says the neck area feels different. Outer skin versus inside the throat remains unclear, and I haven’t observed it. I won’t judge it normal; I’d like to discuss necessary checks.’

Distinguish the person questioned from the report recipient. This asks neither for a disease name nor for diagnostic or first-aid techniques. In real urgent changes, immediately prioritize help and emergency requests over continuing questions.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-merged-transfe.heading: From checking conditions to the person’s new choice
paragraphs: [Staged learning situation] Morikawa-san chose a song, but participation is undecided. They want support for returning to the room at 2:25 p.m. confirmed before deciding. Do not report later-stage information as already known earlier.
At stage one, ask the condition: ‘Would you like to decide after we confirm help returning to your room at 2:25 p.m.?’ The reply is, ‘If I can’t return then, I won’t participate today.’

At stage two, tell Kawase the conditions and unknowns: ‘Morikawa-san wants return support for 2:25 p.m. checked before deciding. They do not want to join if unable to return then. Support and return timing are unconfirmed, and the activity has not started. Please check.’
Kawase replies, ‘Kishimoto will help them return at 2:25 p.m. We haven’t heard their participation decision yet.’ This confirms future support, not completed return.
At stage three, explain results and ask current choice: ‘Kawase-san confirmed Kishimoto will help you return at 2:25 p.m. The activity has not started. Would you like to join on that basis?’
Morikawa-san replies, ‘The time works, but I won’t join today. I’ll just choose the song.’ Meeting conditions does not establish consent to participate.

Stage-four report example: ‘I explained support and the planned 2:25 p.m. return. Morikawa-san chose a song but decided not to join today. The activity has not started. Song choice alone does not establish the whole goal achieved; review will be discussed with the person and team.’

Kawase replies that song choice and nonparticipation will be shared separately and any need for plan review discussed with the person and team. Staff do not independently change goals or label declining participation a failure.

kaigo-review-01-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
希望（きぼう） — Wishes: what the person would like to do or have happen.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.
相談（そうだん） — Seeking advice or support by talking about difficulties or things that are unclear.
移動（いどう） — Mobility: moving between places for a purpose in everyday life.
参加（さんか） — Participation: joining an activity. Distinguish available conditions from the person’s choice to join.
未確認（みかくにん） — Unconfirmed: not yet checked. It does not mean no problem exists.
Useful expression: You’d like to join for a little while. Is there anything you want checked about returning early?
Useful expression: I’ll check the return time too and ask whether it fits your wishes. I’ll also communicate your choice not to join if it does not fit.

kaigo-review-01-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] Morikawa-san wants to hear a little music but not stay until the end. They want return support and timing checked before deciding. They remain in their room; neither departure nor participation is decided. This is not practice in actual transport.
Haruko Morikawa: I’d like to hear a little of today’s performance, but I don’t think I’ll stay until the end.
Care worker Tanaka: You’d like to join for a little while. Is there anything you want checked about returning early?
Haruko Morikawa: I’m worried if return help isn’t arranged. I want to decide after knowing that.
Care worker Tanaka: You’d like to decide after return support is clear. We won’t leave now; I’ll check the plan with the person responsible.
Haruko Morikawa: Yes. If the return time doesn’t suit me, I won’t go today.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll check the return time too and ask whether it fits your wishes. I’ll also communicate your choice not to join if it does not fit.
Haruko Morikawa: Please do. Talk to me again once the plan is clear.
Care worker Tanaka: After sharing the consultation result, I’ll ask again whether you want to join. I won’t record participation as decided yet.

kaigo-review-01-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs: Participation consultation note: Morikawa-san is considering hearing music briefly. They want return assistance and timing checked before deciding. Staff checks are still to come. No departure or participation decision yet.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
希望（きぼう） — Wishes: what the person would like to do or have happen.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.
相談（そうだん） — Seeking advice or support by talking about difficulties or things that are unclear.
参加（さんか） — Participation: joining an activity. Distinguish available conditions from the person’s choice to join.
未確認（みかくにん） — Unconfirmed: not yet checked. It does not mean no problem exists.
報告（ほうこく） — Report: communicate confirmed facts, actions, results or changes.
介護過程（かいごかてい） — Care process: considering information and connecting planning, implementation and evaluation for the life the person wants.
アセスメント（アセスメント） — Assessment: gathering personal information and analyzing daily-life issues and support needs.
介護計画（かいごけいかく） — Care plan: a plan summarizing goals and specific support.
実施（じっし） — Implementation: actually providing support according to the plan, distinct from scheduled action.
評価（ひょうか） — Evaluation: comparing personal outcomes with goals and considering support suitability.
Useful expression: I’ll report what was done separately from outcomes against the goals.
Useful expression: I’d like to check current wishes and discuss reviewing the plan.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] With Kawase-san, review Morikawa-san’s reading-support record. The goal was choosing a favorite book and sharing impressions if participation was wanted. Staff prepared large-print books and a quiet seat under the plan. The person chose one, then wanted to read alone, so no sharing occurred. No new plan is decided.
Naoto Kawase: Let’s review today’s reading record. What goal did the plan set?
Care worker Tanaka: Morikawa-san choosing a favorite book and discussing impressions if they wanted to participate.
Naoto Kawase: Tell me staff actions separately from Morikawa-san’s response.
Care worker Tanaka: We prepared large-print books and a quiet seat according to the plan. Morikawa-san chose one book, then said they wanted to read alone.
Naoto Kawase: Did the impressions-sharing activity take place afterward?
Care worker Tanaka: No. Book choice is confirmed, but I won’t record the entire goal achieved.
Naoto Kawase: We need to check with Morikawa-san and the team whether support matches current wishes.
Care worker Tanaka: Yes. I’ll report their words and support provided and consult about review. I won’t change the plan alone.
Naoto Kawase: First, we’ll share the record and arrange a chance to check with Morikawa-san. No review outcome is decided yet.

kaigo-gap-care-process-01-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs: Reading support record: Prepared large-print books and a quiet seat under the plan. Morikawa-san chose one, then said, ‘I want to read alone.’ No subsequent sharing of impressions. Reported to Kawase and discussed reviewing the plan with the person and team. New goals and support are not decided yet.

kaigo-review-02-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
担当（たんとう） — Being responsible for a particular task or for supporting a person receiving care.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.
共有（きょうゆう） — Sharing information: making sure the relevant people have a common understanding of necessary information.
内容（ないよう） — Content: the matters included in speech, writing or other communication.
連絡（れんらく） — Passing on information to the appropriate person.
同意（どうい） — Consent: understanding and accepting what has been explained. It does not necessarily include agreement to another action.
Useful expression: You’d like record photos by private message. I’ll check what content and methods can be shared.
Useful expression: I’ll tell the responsible person you want photos and that consent to content and method is unknown. I won’t send anything here now.

kaigo-review-02-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] Megumi asks for photos of her mother’s activity record by private message. Only consent to discussion in a meeting with responsible staff is confirmed. Photo sharing and its method remain unconfirmed; nothing has been sent.
Megumi Morikawa: I’d like my mother’s activity record. Could you photograph it and send it to my private messages?
Care worker Tanaka: You’d like record photos by private message. I’ll check what content and methods can be shared.
Megumi Morikawa: Mother said it could be discussed at a meeting with the person responsible. Does that allow sending?
Care worker Tanaka: The current check sheet shows consent to discussion in that meeting. Consent to photos sent by that method is not confirmed yet.
Megumi Morikawa: Then please ask the person responsible, including whether to send. I’d like my mother asked too.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll tell the responsible person you want photos and that consent to content and method is unknown. I won’t send anything here now.
Megumi Morikawa: Understood. Please explain the result at a meeting.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll also pass on that preferred way of receiving results. I won’t promise delivery before checking or record it as sent.

kaigo-review-02-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs: Sharing check sheet: Consent to discussion of activities in a meeting with the responsible staff member. Record photos and private messages unconfirmed. Megumi wants the result at a meeting. No photos sent.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
介護職員（かいごしょくいん） — Care worker: a staff member who provides necessary help with daily activities and supports the person’s everyday life.
担当（たんとう） — Being responsible for a particular task or for supporting a person receiving care.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.
共有（きょうゆう） — Sharing information: making sure the relevant people have a common understanding of necessary information.
報告（ほうこく） — Report: communicate confirmed facts, actions, results or changes.
虐待（ぎゃくたい） — Abuse: acts infringing personal rights, involving not only physical harm but psychological harm, neglect and other forms.
通報（つうほう） — Notification: informing an authorized body of applicable facts or suspicions, distinct from internal reporting.
市町村（しちょうそん） — Municipality: a city, town or village authority. Here, learn it as the notification destination for applicable elder abuse.
Useful expression: I’ll report the words I heard separately from what the person told me.
Useful expression: I’ll promptly notify the municipality separately from the internal report.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] At an older-adult care facility, at 10:05 in the lounge, you hear a worker tell Hasebe-san, ‘If you call again, you won’t get lunch.’ The person is frightened and wants someone present. You call help; another worker is now with them. Injury and actual meal provision are unconfirmed. This is a report to Kawase; municipal notification is not yet made. The speaker is not identified as an existing colleague character.
Naoto Kawase: I received the contact. Where and what did you hear concerning Hasebe-san?
Care worker Tanaka: At 10:05 in the lounge, I heard a worker tell Hasebe-san they would not get lunch if they called again.
Naoto Kawase: What does Hasebe-san say? Who is with them now?
Care worker Tanaka: They said they were frightened and wanted someone present. I called for help, and another worker is with them now.
Naoto Kawase: Tell me unknowns too.
Care worker Tanaka: Injury and whether lunch was actually withheld are unknown. I won’t record unobserved matters as checked.
Naoto Kawase: I’ll check safety. We must not stop at internal reporting; prompt municipal notification is also needed.
Care worker Tanaka: Municipal notification has not occurred yet. I’ll promptly notify them now, separating heard words, the person’s account, responses and unknowns.

kaigo-gap-abuse-report-01-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs:
Practice record: At 10:05 in the lounge, heard a worker tell Hasebe-san lunch would be withheld if they called again. The person was frightened and wanted someone present. Help called; another worker accompanying. Injury and lunch provision unknown. Reported to Kawase; municipality not yet notified.
Separate ordinary consultation: Morikawa-san consents to activity-record explanation at a meeting with the responsible worker. Photos to the daughter and meeting recording are unknown. Neither sending nor recording performed.

kaigo-review-03-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.
予定表（よていひょう） — Schedule: planned activities and times. Distinguish it from a record of completed actions.
洗濯物（せんたくもの） — Laundry: items awaiting washing or already washed. Check the processing stage too.
掲示（けいじ） — Notice: displaying information visibly, or the document displayed.
変更（へんこう） — Change: alter something decided. Also check what remains unchanged.
申し送り（もうしおくり） — Handoff: communicate and check conditions, responses and unfinished matters with the next worker to continue support.
Useful expression: The notice says ‘from October 25.’ Today is the 24th, so I’ll check today’s slip separately from the effective date.
Useful expression: I’ll hand over the old storage room for today, the 24th, and the new one from tomorrow, the 25th. If other instructions are unclear, I’ll check with staff.

kaigo-review-03-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] On October 24, you check a laundry collection slip with Kishimoto-san. Today’s slip names the old storage room; a notice names the new room from the 25th. Practice effective dates, not independently rewriting procedures or moving items.
Misaki Kishimoto: Should we change today’s October 24 laundry collection point to the new storage room already?
Care worker Tanaka: The notice says ‘from October 25.’ Today is the 24th, so I’ll check today’s slip separately from the effective date.
Misaki Kishimoto: Today’s slip says old storage, while the notice says new storage. Aren’t they contradictory?
Care worker Tanaka: They apply to different days. The 24th slip means old storage; from the 25th, new storage. I won’t independently rewrite today’s slip.
Misaki Kishimoto: Understood. Let’s tell tomorrow’s worker the date together with the place.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll hand over the old storage room for today, the 24th, and the new one from tomorrow, the 25th. If other instructions are unclear, I’ll check with staff.

kaigo-review-03-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs:
Collection slip: October 24, old storage room.
Change notice: Posted October 24. Collection changes to new storage from October 25. The 24th collection point is unchanged.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
希望（きぼう） — Wishes: what the person would like to do or have happen.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.
相談（そうだん） — Seeking advice or support by talking about difficulties or things that are unclear.
掲示（けいじ） — Notice: displaying information visibly, or the document displayed.
申し送り（もうしおくり） — Handoff: communicate and check conditions, responses and unfinished matters with the next worker to continue support.
身体拘束（しんたいこうそく） — Restraint: restricting personal freedom of action. It is prohibited in principle and not carried out based only on family requests.
切迫性（せっぱくせい） — Imminence: a very high likelihood of danger to the person’s or another person’s life or body.
非代替性（ひだいたいせい） — Lack of alternatives: no method other than restraint or a similar restriction is available. Check carefully as an organization.
一時性（いちじせい） — Temporary duration: the restriction is temporary. A brief duration does not remove other requirements.
Useful expression: This is a family request, but nothing has been implemented.
Useful expression: I’d like to discuss nonrestrictive support with the person and relevant professionals.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for this material] At 1:40 p.m., Megumi asks for her mother Morikawa-san’s room to be locked from tonight so she cannot go out. It is a request; locking has not occurred. Personal wishes, specific danger, alternatives and organizational decisions are unknown. Consult Kawase without promising implementation. Do not add a diagnosis such as dementia.
Naoto Kawase: Megumi asked for her mother’s room to be locked tonight. What was the request?
Care worker Tanaka: At 1:40 p.m., she requested locking from tonight to prevent leaving. It has not been done.
Naoto Kawase: Do we know the person’s wishes or specific danger?
Care worker Tanaka: Both are unconfirmed. Support alternatives to locking have not been considered yet either.
Naoto Kawase: Family requests alone do not justify restricting action. Let’s consider support with the person.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll share Megumi’s concern and check personal wishes and safety. I’d like to consult relevant professionals about nonrestrictive support.
Naoto Kawase: Whether this is an unavoidable emergency needs careful organizational consideration of requirements and procedures.
Care worker Tanaka: I won’t decide alone or promise locking. I’ll record the request, nonimplementation and unknowns separately and continue consultation.

kaigo-gap-restraint-01-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs:
Practice consultation form (October 26): At 1:40 p.m., Megumi requested locking her mother’s room from tonight to prevent leaving. Not performed. Personal wishes, specific danger and alternatives unconfirmed. Consulting Kawase.
Practice notice (posted October 26): Routine forms go to the consultation room from the 27th; on the 26th, still the staff room. This does not instruct delaying today’s safety contact until tomorrow.

kaigo-review-04-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.
観察（かんさつ） — Observation: carefully checking the person and surroundings.
記録（きろく） — Record: keeping confirmed information and completed actions so they can be understood later.
未確認（みかくにん） — Unconfirmed: not yet checked. It does not mean no problem exists.
口腔ケア（こうくうケア） — Oral care: care supporting cleanliness and health of the mouth, including teeth and gums.
皮膚（ひふ） — Skin: tissue covering the body, involved in protection, sensation and temperature regulation.
Useful expression: Outer skin versus inside the mouth is unclear. I’d like to check with the person without assuming the place.
Useful expression: I’ll preserve their words and record detailed location and observations as unknown, then consult the responsible worker.

kaigo-review-04-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Practice situation created for this material] With nurse Fujino, consider ‘Around my mouth feels different’ in a fictional record. Outer skin versus inside is unknown, and nothing has been observed. This teaches questions and records, not actual examination or symptom assessment.
Aya Fujino: The practice slip says, ‘Around my mouth feels different.’ What would you check first?
Care worker Tanaka: Outer skin versus inside the mouth is unclear. I’d like to check with the person without assuming the place.
Aya Fujino: We haven’t looked yet. Think of one question for the person.
Care worker Tanaka: I’d ask, ‘Does it feel different outside your mouth or inside?’ I won’t record unobserved conditions as normal.
Aya Fujino: Let’s practice that. If the location remains unclear afterward, how will you record it?
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll preserve their words and record detailed location and observations as unknown, then consult the responsible worker.

kaigo-review-04-reading.heading: Read records
paragraphs: Practice record: Person says, ‘Around my mouth feels different.’ Outer skin versus inside mouth unconfirmed. No observation. No normal/abnormal judgment. Consultation with staff planned.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-words.heading: Reference glossary and useful expressions
paragraphs: [Reference glossary] Do not memorize everything at once. Choose needed words today, checking meanings and readings, and look up others as needed.
住所（じゅうしょ） — Address: information indicating where someone lives.
相談（そうだん） — Seeking advice or support by talking about difficulties or things that are unclear.
連絡（れんらく） — Passing on information to the appropriate person.
右（みぎ） — Right: one side of the body or an object. State whose perspective defines right.
年齢（ねんれい） — Age: years since birth.
接続（せつぞく） — Connection: reaching the recipient by phone or another means, distinct from only placing a call.
呼びかけ（よびかけ） — Calling to someone: speaking to get their attention. A reply does not rule out every emergency.
Useful expression: It hasn’t connected yet. Please use another phone.
Useful expression: Contact has been made, but we are still responding under instructions.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-dialog.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Offline training situation] At 9:36, Hasebe-san suddenly has difficulty exerting force in the right arm but responds when called. The first 119 call is unconnected; Kishimoto has another phone. The fictional location is Hidamari Care, second-floor lounge,4-8-2 Higashimachi, Sakura Ward, Tokyo. Neither facility nor address is an actual emergency location. Do not actually call. Kishimoto reads colleague training cards, not the dispatcher role.
Misaki Kishimoto: Here is a training card: sudden right-arm weakness; the first 119 call has not connected. What next?
Care worker Tanaka: Emergency contact is not established yet. Kishimoto-san, please call 119 immediately from another phone. I’ll stay beside Hasebe-san and respond.
Misaki Kishimoto: I’ll practice the other-phone role. What location will you give?
Care worker Tanaka: The fictional address is 4-8-2 Higashimachi, Sakura Ward, Tokyo, Hidamari Care. Hasebe-san is in the second-floor lounge.
Misaki Kishimoto: How will you describe known conditions rather than a disease name?
Care worker Tanaka: At 9:36, I noticed sudden difficulty exerting force in the right arm. They respond to their name. Cause and age are unconfirmed.
Misaki Kishimoto: The next card says 119 connected and instructions are being followed. Distinguish it from the previous state.
Care worker Tanaka: The first call did not connect. Connection was then confirmed through Kishimoto-san’s other phone. Response is ongoing under instructions; contact alone does not mean completion.

kaigo-gap-emergency-call-state-01-readin.heading: Read records
paragraphs:
Training card: At 9:36, Hasebe-san has sudden right-arm weakness and responds when called. First 119 call unconnected. Next card: Kishimoto confirms connection with another phone; response ongoing under instructions. Fictional cards; do not actually call.
Separate ordinary dialogue: Onodera-san reports an unusual mouth-area sensation. Outer skin versus inside is unclear and unobserved. Ask which area they mean. This is separate from the right-arm case; do not record unobserved conditions as normal.

kaigo-language-transfer-263.heading: Read event and preparation dates and times
paragraphs: Autumn event: November 3,2:00 p.m., East Hall. Staff prepare from 1:30 p.m.
The event is November 3 at 2:00 p.m. in East Hall. Staff preparation starts at 1:30 p.m., distinct from the event start.

kaigo-language-transfer-251.heading: Separate visitor identity and schedules
paragraphs: The younger sister visits Saturday mornings. A friend usually visits once a month in the afternoon. This week’s friend visit is undecided.
The younger sister visits Saturday mornings. The friend usually comes monthly in the afternoon, but this week is undecided. A usual habit does not guarantee this week’s visit.

kaigo-language-transfer-264.heading: Distinguish scheduled and actual times
paragraphs: Day-shift schedule: Handoff at 9:00, preparation at 10:00 and recording at 11:00. Enter actual action times separately.
11:00 is the planned recording time. Actual times are entered separately, so the schedule does not establish that recording happened at 11:00.

kaigo-language-transfer-269.heading: Read events across midnight
paragraphs: 9:00 p.m.: Person reported feeling unwell. Food intake unconfirmed.2:00 a.m. the following day: Vomited a little. Nurse contacted.

At 9:00 p.m., the person reported feeling unwell; food intake was unknown. Slight vomiting occurred at 2:00 a.m. the following day, followed by nurse contact. Do not add zero intake or vomiting since 9:00 p.m.

The weekly content check is separate and does not replace the full mock. Check saving and submission too, without marking unperformed work complete.

kaigo-review-02.context: [Situation created for this material] Megumi asks for photos of her mother’s activity record by private message. Only consent to discussion in a meeting with responsible staff is confirmed. Photo sharing and its method remain unconfirmed; nothing has been sent.

Outer skin versus inside is unknown, and nothing has been observed. This teaches questions and records, not actual examination or symptom assessment.

weekly-review-q01.prompt: What matters when checking participation wishes?
options: Treat everyone as attending because an event exists.
Ask about conditions as well as wishes.
Omit the wish to return early.
Promise return help before asking staff.
rationales: An event does not prove everyone’s consent.
Check wishes together with conditions such as early return.
Early-return wishes are important participation conditions.
Do not promise unchecked support.
weekly-review-q01.reading: Participation consultation note: Morikawa-san is considering hearing music briefly. They want return assistance and timing checked before deciding. Staff checks are still to come. No departure or participation decision yet.

weekly-review-q02.prompt: What does Morikawa-san want to know before deciding?
options: The performer’s address.
Tomorrow’s menu.
All participants’ medical histories.
Support for returning.
rationales: No performer-address request is made.
Tomorrow’s menu is not this condition.
Other participants’ histories are not requested.
They want return support clear before deciding.
weekly-review-q02.reading:
[Situation created for this material] Morikawa-san wants to hear a little music but not stay until the end. They want return support and timing checked before deciding. They remain in their room; neither departure nor participation is decided. This is not practice in actual transport.
Haruko Morikawa: I’d like to hear a little of today’s performance, but I don’t think I’ll stay until the end.
Care worker Tanaka: You’d like to join for a little while. Is there anything you want checked about returning early?
Haruko Morikawa: I’m worried if return help isn’t arranged. I want to decide after knowing that.
Care worker Tanaka: You’d like to decide after return support is clear. We won’t leave now; I’ll check the plan with the person responsible.
Haruko Morikawa: Yes. If the return time doesn’t suit me, I won’t go today.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll check the return time too and ask whether it fits your wishes. I’ll also communicate your choice not to join if it does not fit.
Haruko Morikawa: Please do. Talk to me again once the plan is clear.
Care worker Tanaka: After sharing the consultation result, I’ll ask again whether you want to join. I won’t record participation as decided yet.

weekly-review-q03.prompt: What is correct at the note’s time?
options: Checking with staff is still to come.
Participation is confirmed.
Departure is complete.
Return assistance was performed.
rationales: Staff checks, participation and departure are still pending.
They want to decide after checking; participation is undecided.
Departure has not occurred.
Return arrangements are unchecked, not performed.
weekly-review-q03.reading: Participation consultation note: Morikawa-san is considering hearing music briefly. They want return assistance and timing checked before deciding. Staff checks are still to come. No departure or participation decision yet.

weekly-review-q04.prompt: The return time does not match the person’s wishes. What is appropriate?
options: Decide by staff convenience alone.
Hide the choice not to participate.
Check the person’s choice and tell staff.
Change the condition to staying until the end.
rationales: Staff convenience alone does not decide participation.
Communicate declining participation too.
Check the person’s choice when conditions do not fit and communicate it to the person responsible.
Staff must not replace the condition with staying throughout.
weekly-review-q04.reading: Participation consultation note: Morikawa-san is considering hearing music briefly. They want return assistance and timing checked before deciding. Staff checks are still to come. No departure or participation decision yet.

weekly-review-q05.prompt: Early-exit conditions remain unknown. What is appropriate?
options: Promise to manage alone and depart.
Check exit support first, then discuss with the person.
Refuse all future participation for anyone with conditions.
Record participation before consulting.
rationales: Independent ability is unknown; do not promise and depart.
Check support, explain results and consult the person.
Today’s conditions do not decide every future activity.
Participation has not happened and cannot be recorded complete.
weekly-review-q05.reading: Participation consultation note: Morikawa-san is considering hearing music briefly. They want return assistance and timing checked before deciding. Staff checks are still to come. No departure or participation decision yet.

weekly-review-q06.prompt: What follows from consent to discuss at a meeting?
options: Records may be posted on personal social media.
Photos may be sent by any method.
Meeting consent and photo-sharing consent need separate checks.
Family sharing needs no information-management checks.
rationales: Meeting consent does not extend to public posting.
Photo sharing requires separate checks including method.
Check the different actions and methods separately.
Family sharing still needs scope and method checks.
weekly-review-q06.reading: Sharing check sheet: Consent to discussion of activities in a meeting with the responsible staff member. Record photos and private messages unconfirmed. Megumi wants the result at a meeting. No photos sent.

weekly-review-q07.prompt: What receiving method did Megumi initially request?
options: Record photos by private message.
A public notice.
Publication outside the facility.
A mailed medical certificate.
rationales: The initial request is private-message photos.
A public notice was not requested.
No external publication request is made.
This is not a medical-certificate mailing request.
weekly-review-q07.reading:
[Situation created for this material] Megumi asks for photos of her mother’s activity record by private message. Only consent to discussion in a meeting with responsible staff is confirmed. Photo sharing and its method remain unconfirmed; nothing has been sent.
Megumi Morikawa: I’d like my mother’s activity record. Could you photograph it and send it to my private messages?
Care worker Tanaka: You’d like record photos by private message. I’ll check what content and methods can be shared.
Megumi Morikawa: Mother said it could be discussed at a meeting with the person responsible. Does that allow sending?
Care worker Tanaka: The current check sheet shows consent to discussion in that meeting. Consent to photos sent by that method is not confirmed yet.
Megumi Morikawa: Then please ask the person responsible, including whether to send. I’d like my mother asked too.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll tell the responsible person you want photos and that consent to content and method is unknown. I won’t send anything here now.
Megumi Morikawa: Understood. Please explain the result at a meeting.
Care worker Tanaka: I’ll also pass on that preferred way of receiving results. I won’t promise delivery before checking or record it as sent.

weekly-review-q08.prompt: What remains unconfirmed on the check sheet?
options: Consent to discussion in a meeting.
That photos have not been sent.
The wish to hear results at a meeting.
Record-photo delivery and private-message use.
rationales: Meeting-discussion consent is confirmed.
Unsent status is known.
The preferred result explanation is confirmed.
Consent to photos and private messages remains unconfirmed.
weekly-review-q08.reading: Sharing check sheet: Consent to discussion of activities in a meeting with the responsible staff member. Record photos and private messages unconfirmed. Megumi wants the result at a meeting. No photos sent.

options: Send first, then ask consent.
Tell staff the request and unknowns.
Promise definite delivery.
Record sent despite no sending.
rationales: Checking afterward means sharing while unknown.
Tell the person responsible the wishes and unconfirmed matters so they can be checked.
Do not promise before confirmation.
Unsent items cannot be recorded as sent.
weekly-review-q09.reading: Sharing check sheet: Consent to discussion of activities in a meeting with the responsible staff member. Record photos and private messages unconfirmed. Megumi wants the result at a meeting. No photos sent.

weekly-review-q10.prompt: Family wants to record the meeting. What is appropriate?
options: Automatically record because meeting consent exists.
Record without checking on a family phone.
Check recording consent and facility procedures separately.
Record before informing the person.
rationales: Meeting and recording consent differ.
Family devices do not remove recording checks.
